abstract: The conserved oligomeric Golgi (COG) complex tethers retrograde intra-Golgi transport vesicles, but how it engages the SNARE machinery to support vesicle fusion remains unclear. Here, we identify a functional interface between the COG subunit COG4 and the Qa-SNARE Syntaxin 5 (STX5). The C-terminal region of COG4 coprecipitated with STX5, and AlphaFold3 modeling placed the COG4 MUN-C-like subdomain in contact with the STX5 Ha-Hb loop and the linker connecting its Habc domain to the SNARE motif. Replacing the Ha-Hb loop with a flexible Gly/Ser sequence preserved STX5 localization and its interaction with SCFD1 but impaired rescue of GPP130 abundance and protein glycosylation in STX5-depleted cells. Combining the loop replacement with linker substitutions reduced recovery of COG3 and the SNARE partner GS15 with STX5 and led to vesicle accumulation around disorganized Golgi cisternae. On the COG4 side of the interface with Qa-SNARE, alanine substitution of the conserved residues D452 and D453 reduced coprecipitation with STX5. Replacing these residues with either alanine or lysine preserved COG4 localization and COG8 recruitment to the Golgi but failed to restore normal glycosylation, GS15 localization, or altered Golgi morphology in COG4-knockout cells. These findings support a model in which the COG4-STX5 interface couples vesicle tethering to productive SNARE assembly, thereby controlling vesicular retrograde trafficking and Golgi organization.
